lead.label: Climate · COP31
lead.headline: Bangladesh asks COP31 for three times more adaptation finance
lead.summary: The Prime Minister met President Erdogan in Antalya and speaks to the plenary on 12 November. Dhaka wants grants, not loans.

alsoToday.label: Governance · NGOs
alsoToday.headline: 722 NGOs lost registration in 15 years, minister tells Parliament
alsoToday.summary: Late renewals, forged donor letters and misused grants were among the reasons. The government says it will stay strict.

special.label: Special report · Workforce
special.headline: After the USAID cuts, where did 50,000 development workers go?
special.summary: No official count, no support scheme. Our analysis traces what happened to the people who lost their jobs after the aid cuts.

pinnedSpecials.label: Special report · Funding Intelligence
pinnedSpecials.headline: Record pledges, shrinking NGOs: who gets Bangladesh's aid money
pinnedSpecials.summary: Foreign grants to NGOs are at a seven-year high, yet about 2,200 small NGOs face cuts. Our analysis of six years of data shows the money is reaching fewer, larger organisations.

spotlight.label: Spotlight
spotlight.title: COP31 in Antalya
spotlight.intro: Bangladesh is asking for grant-based adaptation money and loss and damage support, not more loans. Devlens follows what the summit means for the sector until the talks close.

today.text: Day 2 focuses on energy security and transport. The leaders' segment runs on 11 and 12 November, and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is in Antalya until 12 November.

watch: Adaptation finance: whether the COP30 pledge to at least triple it by 2035 gets a baseline, an amount and a delivery plan.
Adaptation indicators: how countries put the 59 Global Goal on Adaptation indicators into practice.
Just transition: whether a mechanism is set up in Antalya, and what it covers.
